title: Compact Cost Explorer (opt-in) with Deferred Trace Linking — scope reduction & acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: The original Console roadmap included a full Cost Explorer with per-request tracing, flamegraphs, and detailed per-token cost timelines. To hit the console-2026.03 ship window and reduce ingestion/back-end complexity, we are narrowing scope to an opt-in Compact Cost Explorer. This will expose per-route cost summaries, aggregated token category breakdowns, and the top three cost drivers (model, route, and heavy requests). Deep trace ingestion, full request flamegraphs, and per-token timelines are being deferred to the next cycle.
acceptance_criteria: Compact Cost Explorer UI is available behind an org-level feature flag (opt-in)
Per-route cost card shows 7-day and 30-day aggregated cost, request count, and avg cost per request
Token breakdown displays categories (prompt / completion / embeddings) with percentages and absolute token counts
Top-3 cost drivers list is populated with model, route, and a sampled request signature (no full trace payload)
Lightweight trace anchors (trace id + timestamp + small metadata) are shown instead of full trace visualization
Backend ingestion rate for telemetry is reduced by at least 40% compared to the full-trace plan (measured on a staging workload) or within infra budget targets
Docs updated: quickstart for enabling opt-in, data retention expectations, and upgrade path to full trace linking
Basic alerting on missing telemetry: if route cost <expected coverage> for 48h, console surfaces a warning
decision_log: Stakeholders: PM (Aisha), Product Design (Maya Rivera), Infra/Telemetry (Liam, Priya), Runtime/Serving leads (Jorge). Trade-offs: preserve earliest shipping of actionable cost signals versus delaying rich trace UX. Chosen approach reduces storage/query complexity (no high-cardinality full traces) while giving customers an opt-in path to deeper investigations. Agreed on clear upgrade path and visible telemetry caveats in UI.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal dogfood + two pilot customers enabled (week 1). Phase 2: opt-in org-level beta (gradual enablement across accounts, week 2-4). Phase 3: GA opt-in with docs and SDK snippets (post validation). Feature flag controls shipped with console-2026.03; can be toggled per-org. Monitor: adoption rate, query latency, telemetry ingress, and false-negative coverage of heavy-cost routes.
notes: Related docs and artifacts: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Compact+Cost+Explorer+Spec (draft). Design Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/Cost-Explorer-Compact. GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/6203 (backend schema). Staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/console-costs/compact-explorer (permissions required).
qa_checks: Enable org feature flag and verify Compact Cost Explorer appears in left nav
Validate per-route cost numbers match aggregated values from billing export (allow 2% tolerance)
Confirm token category breakdown calculation matches offline aggregation job
Ensure trace anchors link to existing audit logs but do not surface full trace payload
Load test with synthetic workload to validate ingestion budget target and query latency SLAs
